speaker_role: current admission staff at University of Richmond (several unnamed staff, interviewed by a student host)
key_insights: Use a genuine voice and let real passion for the subject show.
Start early; staff say they can tell when an essay was rushed.
If unsure which Common App prompt to use, write a little for each and see which one pulls you in.
Give a trusted reader the draft and ask for a one-sentence summary, because officers reduce an essay to roughly one sentence for the committee.
Avoid over-editing that erases your voice, and avoid going for shock value or showcasing trauma for effect.
Get the school name right, e.g. Richmond or UR, to avoid a copy-paste mistake.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Staff say committee presenters boil essays down to a one-sentence summary (stated by a Richmond staffer).
notable_or_distinctive: The one-sentence-summary test tied to how essays are relayed within committee.
reliability_notes: Short soundbite video from one school's staff; mostly generic and specific to Richmond's process.
